'''''Ravenala madagascariensis''''', commonly known as the '''traveller's tree''', '''fan palm''', '''traveller's palm''' or '''East-West palm''', is a species of [[monocotyledonous]] flowering plant found in Madagascar. It is not a true palm but a member of the family [[Strelitziaceae]]. In tropical and subtropical regions, the plant is widely cultivated for its distinctive habit and foliage.{{cn |date=October 2025}}

== Name ==
It has been given the name "traveller's palm" because the sheaths of the stems hold rainwater, which supposedly could be used as an emergency drinking supply for needy travellers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.floridata.com/ref/R/rave_mad.cfm |title=Ravenala madagascariensis |publisher=Floridata.com |access-date=September 14, 2009 |date=May 16, 2000 |author=McLendon, Chuck}}</ref> Another plausible reason for its name is that the fan tends to grow on an east–west line, providing a crude compass.

== Description ==
The enormous paddle-shaped leaves are borne on long [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]], in a distinctive [[hand fan|fan]] shape aligned in a single plane ([[Phyllotaxy|distichous]]). The foliar fan consists of 30 to 45 leaves for mature specimens, each as much as 36 feet (11 metres) in length.<ref>{{cite web |title=Protabase Published species |url=http://database.prota.org/publishedspeciesEn.htm |access-date=2010-04-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100504125220/http://database.prota.org/publishedspeciesEn.htm |archive-date=2010-05-04 }}  Then click "Ravenala madagascariensis"</ref> As the plant grows older, it progressively loses the lowest or oldest leaves and reveals a sturdy grey trunk. Of the four forms, varieties or subspecies, the largest is the "Bemavo", from the hills of eastern Madagascar, which can be 100 feet (30 metres) in height with a trunk 2 feet (60 cm) thick.<ref>Das Pflanzenreich Volume 4 Issue 45 (1900) page 29</ref> 

The large white flowers are structurally similar to those of its relatives, the bird-of-paradise flowers ''[[Strelitzia reginae]]'' and ''[[Strelitzia nicolai]]'', but are generally considered less attractive, with a green [[bract]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Calley|first1=M.|last2=Braithwaite|first2=R. W.|last3=Ladd|first3=P. G.|year=1993|title=Reproductive Biology of ''Ravenala madagascariensis'' Gmel. as an Alien Species|journal=Biotropica|volume=25|issue=1|pages=61–72|doi=10.2307/2388979|jstor=2388979|bibcode=1993Biotr..25...61C }}</ref> These flowers, upon being pollinated, produce brilliant blue seeds. 

The chromosome number is 2n = 22.<ref name="Internet Archive 2016">{{cite web | title=Full text of "Chromosome Atlas Of Flowering Plants Ed. 2nd" | website=Internet Archive | date=2016-10-23 | url=https://archive.org/stream/in.ernet.dli.2015.460004/2015.460004.Chromosome-Atlas_djvu.txt | language=la | access-date=2019-07-09}}</ref>

==Range and habitat==
''Ravenala madagascariensis'' is widespread in Madagascar, including [[Madagascar lowland forests|humid lowland forests]], [[Madagascar subhumid forests|montane forests]], [[grassland]], and rocky areas, from sea level to 1,500 meters elevation.<ref name = iucn/>

==Ecology==
[[Ruffed lemur]]s are a known [[pollinator]] of this plant and given the size and structure of the [[inflorescence]]s, as well as the lemur's selectivity, method of feeding, and long muzzle, this relationship is thought to have [[coevolution|coevolved]].<ref name=Garbutt>{{cite book | last = Garbutt | first = Nick | title = Mammals of Madagascar, A Complete Guide | publisher = A&C Black Publishers | year = 2007 | pages = 170–175 | isbn = 978-0-300-12550-4}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
The plant requires a sunny spot (not full sun until it is larger). It responds well to fertilizer, especially if it is high in nitrogen during the growing season. This produces better growth and foliage. The plant grows to an average height of {{convert|7|m|abbr=on}} and requires moderate water.
